overview: TKO is a premium sports and entertainment company formed in September 2023 through the combination of UFC (mixed martial arts) and WWE (sports entertainment), and majority-controlled by Endeavor Group Holdings (itself controlled by Silver Lake). On February 28, 2025, TKO acquired IMG (global sports marketing/media rights agency), On Location (premium experiential hospitality) and PBR (Professional Bull Riders) from Endeavor in a ~$3.25 billion stock-for-stock deal, transforming TKO from a two-property IP owner into a diversified sports, media-rights-services and hospitality conglomerate. The company reaches more than 1 billion households across over 200 countries and organizes 500+ live events annually, monetizing content through four streams: media rights/production, live events and hospitality, partnerships/marketing, and consumer products licensing.

business_model.summary: TKO monetizes owned sports/entertainment IP (UFC, WWE, PBR) and third-party rights-holder relationships (IMG, On Location) across four revenue streams. Media rights are increasingly the dominant and highest-margin stream, underpinned by long-term (5-10+ year) contracts with major distributors (Paramount+, Netflix, ESPN, Versant/USA, the CW), giving good revenue visibility. Live events/hospitality and consumer products are more transactional/event-driven, while IMG's agency revenue includes pass-through production/commission fees that carry lower margins.

revenue_streams.name: Media rights, production and content
revenue_streams.note: Largest and highest-margin stream; UFC moved from ESPN (~$550M/yr) to a new 7-year, $7.7B (~$1.1B/yr avg) Paramount+ deal starting 2026; WWE has a 10-year, ~$5B Netflix deal (global ex-US rights plus Raw) and a new 5-year, ~$1.6B ESPN deal for Premium Live Events starting Sept 2025

revenue_streams.name: Live events and hospitality
revenue_streams.note: Ticketing, site fees, VIP/travel packages across UFC, WWE, PBR; On Location adds Olympics/FIFA World Cup/Super Bowl hospitality

revenue_streams.name: Partnerships and marketing
revenue_streams.note: In-venue/in-broadcast sponsorship sold directly and, via IMG, on behalf of third-party rights holders (EPL, MLS, Wimbledon, NFL, ATP/WTA, etc.)

revenue_streams.name: Consumer products licensing and other
revenue_streams.note: Video games (EA Sports/Take-Two), toys (Mattel), apparel/merchandise (Fanatics); plus JV management fees (Zuffa Boxing)

segment_mix_fy2025.note: Growth from partnerships/marketing and media rights; Paramount deal step-up begins 2026
Down from $1,970.2M in 2024 due to 2024 Paris Olympics revenue in prior-year comp; event-cycle dependent (Olympics, FIFA World Cup)

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2C (ticket buyers, PPV/streaming subscribers, merchandise consumers) and B2B (distribution partners, corporate sponsors, rights-holder clients of IMG)
business_model.geographic_mix: U.S.-centric revenue recognition but majority of UFC and WWE fans are international; UFC content reaches 950M+ households in 170+ countries, WWE 1B+ households in 150+ countries; live events held across North America, Europe, Middle East (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar), Asia-Pacific and Latin America

main_competitors: ONE Championship, Professional Fighters League, Combate Global (MMA)
All Elite Wrestling (AEW), New Japan Pro-Wrestling (sports entertainment/wrestling)
Endeavor/IMG rivals: CAA, Wasserman, Octagon (sports marketing/representation agencies)
On Location rivals: other premium hospitality/ticketing providers (e.g., CWT Sports, PrimeSport)
Broader competition: NFL/NBA/other major sports leagues and streaming entertainment for discretionary media/live-event spend
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant #1 in global MMA (UFC) and sports entertainment/wrestling (WWE) with no close scale peer in either category; newly expanded into sports marketing/media-rights advisory (IMG) and premium hospitality (On Location), where it is a large player in fragmented markets without a dominant share

moat_factors.factor: Owned, irreplicable IP and talent pipelines
moat_factors.description: UFC and WWE are the clear scale leaders in their categories with decades of brand equity, talent development systems (UFC Performance Institutes, WWE Performance Center/NXT) and no real network of competing promoters

Multi-year deals (Netflix 10yr, Paramount 7yr, ESPN 5yr) lock in escalating, largely fixed-fee revenue and give multi-year visibility; rights values for premium live sports content have risen consistently across renewal cycles
No franchise/owner-operator system (unlike major team sports leagues); unilateral control over content, scheduling and IP lets TKO move faster than federated competitors
IMG and On Location additions let TKO bundle sponsorship, media and hospitality offerings across UFC/WWE/PBR plus third-party rights holders, diversifying beyond owned IP
Younger, more international, more gender-balanced fanbase than traditional U.S. leagues is attractive to advertisers

weaknesses: IMG and On Location operate in highly fragmented, lower-margin, competitively intense markets with no dominant share
Dependent on handful of distribution partners (Paramount, Netflix, ESPN) for the majority of media rights revenue - concentration risk
WWE carries reputational/legal overhang from the Vince McMahon misconduct investigation and related litigation
IMG revenue is lumpy/event-cycle dependent (Olympics, World Cup years create tough comps)
Talent (UFC fighters, WWE Superstars) are independent contractors - risk of reclassification litigation (CA/NY) and retention/compensation pressure

growth_drivers: Step-change increase in U.S. media rights value: UFC's new 7-year, $7.7B Paramount+ deal (~$1.1B/yr) vs. prior ESPN deal (~$550M/yr) roughly doubles UFC's domestic media rights revenue starting 2026
WWE media rights escalation under 10-year Netflix deal (~$5B) and new 5-year ESPN Premium Live Event deal (~$1.6B), replacing Peacock/USA Network arrangements
International expansion of live events and direct-to-consumer platforms (UFC FIGHT PASS, WWE Network) into Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, including Saudi Arabia partnership events

Cross-selling and bundling opportunities from the IMG/On Location/PBR acquisition - expanding into sports marketing services and premium hospitality for marquee events (2026/2028 Olympics, FIFA World Cup 2026)
Zuffa Boxing joint venture (with Sela, launched March 2025) extends TKO's live-event/media infrastructure into professional boxing

Consumer products/licensing growth via video games (EA Sports, Take-Two), toys (Mattel) and e-commerce (Fanatics) partnerships, plus potential expansion into casual games and online betting-adjacent products
Capital return program: $2.0B share buyback authorization (ongoing) and increased quarterly dividend (~$150M/quarter run-rate as of Sept 2025, up from ~$75M)
Site-fee growth as cities compete to host tentpole events (WrestleMania, UFC numbered events) given demonstrated economic impact

business.description: A large share of revenue flows through a small number of distribution partners (Paramount, Netflix, ESPN); loss, non-renewal, or Netflix's contractual opt-out after year 5 of the 10-year deal could materially impair distribution and revenue
IMG revenue fell ~31% YoY in FY2025 due to lapping 2024 Paris Olympics revenue; results are lumpy around major quadrennial events

Dependence on star athletes/performers; WWE's Vince McMahon investigation, related litigation (including a Trafficking Victims Protection Act lawsuit) and potential new claims could affect partner/sponsor relationships
Newly entered sports marketing and hospitality markets are highly fragmented with no dominant competitive position, unlike UFC/WWE

Company may fail to realize anticipated benefits/synergies of the Feb 2025 Endeavor Asset Acquisition (IMG/On Location/PBR); reliance on Transition Services Agreement with Endeavor for key operational functions

financial.description: Total indebtedness of $3.7B as of year-end 2025 (up from $2.735B a year earlier); company has signaled further debt-funded share repurchases, raising balance-sheet risk versus a simple capital-return narrative
TKO Group Holdings depends on distributions from TKO OpCo to pay taxes; tax receivable agreement and partnership audit rules create potential cash-flow mismatches
International live events, licensing and talent costs create FX and repatriation exposure

regulatory.description: Operations require promoter/athlete licenses across many jurisdictions; antitrust/fair competition scrutiny possible given UFC's dominant MMA position
California/New York legislative activity threatens the independent-contractor treatment of UFC fighters and WWE Superstars, which could raise costs materially if reclassified

regulatory.risk: Data privacy / cross-border data transfer regulation
regulatory.description: GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/state privacy laws, China's PIPL/Cybersecurity/Data Security Laws (relevant given UFC Performance Institute in China) create compliance costs and potential fines up to a percentage of global revenue
Supply of betting data/content to gambling operators is subject to jurisdiction-specific licensing

macro.risk: Consumer and corporate discretionary spending sensitivity
macro.description: Revenue depends on discretionary consumer spending (tickets, merchandise, PPV/subscriptions) and corporate sponsorship/advertising budgets, both of which are cyclical and sensitive to recession, inflation and interest rates
International live events expose the company to war, terrorism, sanctions (e.g., Russia/Belarus/Ukraine-related), and visa/immigration policy risk affecting athlete/personnel travel

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Secular tailwind for premium live sports/entertainment media rights: linear, streaming and tech platforms are competing aggressively for scarce premium live content, driving consistent appreciation in rights values across renewal cycles (demonstrated by UFC's ~2x step-up with Paramount and WWE's Netflix/ESPN deals)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - live event attendance, sponsorship/advertising and consumer products spending are discretionary and cyclical, but long-term contracted media rights provide a more stable, recurring revenue base that cushions cyclicality
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - $3.7B+ of debt (with further debt-funded buybacks planned) makes interest expense and refinancing (term loans maturing 2031) sensitive to rate levels; higher rates also pressure consumer discretionary spending

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 results: revenue of $1.36B (+21% YoY), net income $277.9M, adjusted EBITDA $555.7M (41% margin); diluted EPS of $1.33 beat estimates though revenue missed consensus (~$1.37-1.38B); UFC revenue +60% to $519.2M on Paramount step-up, WWE revenue -1% to $399.3M (fewer PLEs in quarter vs. prior year), IMG revenue +16% to $391M aided by FIFA World Cup hospitality via On Location

Full-year 2026 guidance raised for the second time this year: revenue to $5.79-5.83B (from $5.775-5.825B) and adjusted EBITDA to $2.295-2.315B (from $2.275-2.305B); management declined to give 2027 guidance, deferring to Q4 2026 call in February 2027
Management signaled continued use of incremental debt to fund share repurchases, reviving investor concerns about leverage even amid strong operating results

Stock fell to a new 52-week low (~$170) amid analyst caution that 2026 guidance may not justify premium valuation, following a steep decline from the Feb-2026 52-week high (~$227) post-Q4 2025 earnings miss

Board authorized launch of up to $1 billion in additional share repurchases (on top of the existing $2.0B program), funded substantially with new debt and cash on hand; credit facility amended/upsized (~$900M) to support buybacks and dividend

Q4/FY2025 results: FY2025 revenue of $4.735B (down 3% YoY, largely due to IMG lapping 2024 Paris Olympics revenue); WWE +22% to $1.709B, UFC +~7% to $1.502B, IMG -31% to $1.367B; FY2025 net income $546.2M, adjusted EBITDA ~$1.585B; initial 2026 guidance of $5.675-5.775B revenue
Netflix became the new U.S. home for WWE's archival PLE library, documentaries and original programming, consolidating WWE library content under Netflix globally

New 5-year ESPN partnership for WWE Premium Live Events began with Wrestlepalooza, making ESPN's direct-to-consumer platform the exclusive U.S. home for WrestleMania, Royal Rumble, SummerSlam, Survivor Series etc.

UFC announced a new 7-year, ~$7.7B media rights deal with Paramount (Paramount+/CBS) starting 2026 to become the exclusive U.S. home for all UFC events, ending the PPV model domestically; subsequently expanded to cover Latin America and Australia
Board approved an increase to the quarterly dividend program to ~$150M in aggregate quarterly distributions (from ~$75M)
Launched Zuffa Boxing joint venture with Sela Company, a new global professional boxing promotion
Completed the Endeavor Asset Acquisition - acquired IMG, On Location and PBR from Endeavor Group Holdings for ~$3.25B (plus $50M adjustment), paid in TKO OpCo units/Class B shares

items.notes: Raised from $5.775-5.825B (set in August 2026), which itself was raised from the initial $5.675-5.775B given with FY2025 results in February 2026
Raised from $2.275-2.305B; implies ~40% adjusted EBITDA margin
Management explicitly declined to issue 2027 guidance on the Q3 2026 call, deferring to the Q4 2026/full-year earnings call expected February 2027; cited as a near-term source of investor uncertainty

items.target: Up to $1 billion incremental authorization (on top of $2.0B program)
items.notes: To be funded substantially with incremental debt and cash on hand; as of Dec 31, 2025, $866.8M of the original $2.0B program had been executed (4.6M shares)
Increased from ~$75M in September 2025; board retains full discretion to change or discontinue

guidance.management_commentary: Management (CFO Andrew Schleimer) emphasized confidence in the step-up from new UFC (Paramount) and WWE (Netflix/ESPN) media rights deals driving the FY2026 guidance raise, while acknowledging the shift toward debt-funded capital returns. 2027 guidance was explicitly withheld pending the February 2027 call, which some analysts flagged as adding near-term uncertainty despite the EPS beat.

bull_case: Structural step-up in media rights economics: UFC's new Paramount deal roughly doubles U.S. media rights value (~$1.1B/yr vs. ~$550M/yr under ESPN), and WWE's Netflix/ESPN deals lock in long-dated, escalating, largely fixed revenue with minimal variable cost, driving margin expansion

Dominant, hard-to-replicate IP in UFC and WWE with no close competitor at scale, a young/international/diverse fanbase attractive to advertisers, and a structural advantage over franchise-based team sports leagues (no owner-operator network)

Diversification into IMG (sports marketing services) and On Location (premium hospitality) broadens the revenue base beyond owned IP and captures growth from marquee third-party events (Olympics, FIFA World Cup 2026)
Shareholder-friendly capital return program - $2.0B+ buyback authorization plus a growing dividend (~$150M/quarter) - signals management confidence in free cash flow generation
Guidance has been raised twice in 2026, and Q3 2026 EPS beat estimates, suggesting operating momentum ahead of the step-change Paramount revenue recognition beginning in 2026
bear_case: Endeavor/Silver Lake control ~63% of voting power; TKO is a NYSE "controlled company" exempt from several governance protections, and minority stockholders have limited influence over board composition or major transactions

Rising leverage from debt-funded share buybacks ($3.7B+ total debt, up from $2.735B a year earlier) raises balance-sheet risk and could constrain flexibility if a downturn or rights-renewal disappointment occurs

Revenue concentration in a handful of distribution partners (Paramount, Netflix, ESPN); WWE revenue was down YoY in Q3 2026 due to event-schedule timing, and IMG revenue is lumpy around major global sporting events, creating headline volatility

Management's refusal to give 2027 guidance, a Q3 2026 revenue miss versus consensus despite the EPS beat, and a ~25% stock decline from February 2026 highs to an October 2026 52-week low reflect investor skepticism that growth will continue to justify a premium valuation

WWE carries ongoing reputational/legal overhang from the Vince McMahon misconduct investigation and related litigation, plus structural risk from potential reclassification of independent-contractor talent in states like California and New York
